title: Policy Checking vs Policy Comparison: What Brokers Need
summary: Policy checking vs policy comparison: what each catches, when brokers need them across quote, bind, and renewal, and how both reduce E&O risk.
body_markdown:
Policy checking confirms that the policy a carrier issued matches what your client agreed to buy. Policy comparison lines up two or more documents, such as competing quotes or an expiring policy and its renewal, so a broker can advise on the differences. Brokers need both at different points in a placement, and each one protects against a different kind of errors and omissions (E&O) claim.


Commercial pricing softened again in the second quarter of 2026, with average premiums down 2.0% across account sizes, according to[The Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers (CIAB)](https://www.ciab.com/resources/q2-2026-pc-market-survey) . Softer markets bring more remarketing, and Utica National's E&O team estimates that[at least one-third of agency E&O claims](https://risk.uticanational.com/eo/loss-control-articles/at-least-one-third-of-eo-claims-result-from-an-agency-moving-coverage-to-a-new-carrier) involve moving coverage to a new carrier. Every move adds a comparison before the bind and a check after it.


## **Key takeaways**


- Policy checking happens after issuance and has a right answer: the policy either matches the binder, quote, and application, or it doesn't.
- Policy comparison happens before a decision and produces a list of differences that a broker interprets and explains to the client.
- A typical placement involves four related tasks: quote comparison, bind-order verification, policy checking, and renewal comparison.
- Failure to procure coverage is still the No. 1 reason agencies are sued, based on Big "I" Swiss Re E&O program data, and both workflows guard against it.
- Nearly half of independent agencies now use AI, yet a separate Big "I" survey found only 20% use AI in policy comparison tools.


## **What policy checking is**


Policy checking is the review of an issued policy against the documents that came before it: the application, the proposal, the quote, and the binder.[Rough Notes](https://roughnotes.com/mastering-the-fine-art-of-policy-contract-checking) recommends reviewing each policy received against everything in the client file, including previous policies, proposals, applications, and premium comparisons. Big I New York’s[E&O Report](https://biginy.org/eo/TLC/2015/0915.aspx) adds a more specific step: when the policy arrives, check every attached form against the forms listed in the quote or binder.


The checker is looking for discrepancies that shouldn't exist. A misspelled named insured, a missing location, the wrong policy period, a form that was never quoted, or a limit lower than the binder all count.[IA Magazine notes](https://www.iamagazine.com/2025/05/01/whats-driving-the-rise-in-eo-claims-and-what-can-your-agency-do-to-prevent-one/) that carriers sometimes add a vaguely worded endorsement that works as an exclusion. Policy checking is the step that catches it before the client files a claim.


Quality targets are less forgiving than they sound.[Utica National](https://risk.uticanational.com/eo/loss-control-articles/policy-checking-and-delivery) points out that a 95% quality ratio still means one out of every 20 policies contains a mistake. Its guidance is to check promptly, using a saved checklist that covers the named insured, addresses, dates, policy number, and coverage-specific items.


## **What policy comparison is**


Policy comparison puts two or more documents side by side to show where they differ. For brokers, it usually takes one of two forms. Quote comparison lines up competing carrier quotes for the same risk before the client chooses. Renewal comparison lines up the expiring policy against the renewal offer before the client renews.


Comparison rarely has a single correct answer. A higher deductible might be acceptable if the premium drops, and a narrower exclusion might matter to one client and not another. The broker's job is to surface the differences and help the client decide. Utica National recommends a[side-by-side spreadsheet](https://risk.uticanational.com/eo/loss-control-articles/at-least-one-third-of-eo-claims-result-from-an-agency-moving-coverage-to-a-new-carrier) that lists the main coverage issues and shows how each carrier handles them, along with the client’s written acknowledgment of any reduction in coverage.


## **Where each one fits in a placement**


Most brokerages don't run a single "policy review" step. They run four related tasks at different moments, each with its own documents, owner, and failure mode. For a refresher on how the documents relate, see our explainer on the[quote, binder, policy and certificate](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/commercial-insurance-explained) .


‍


Stage Type Documents Compared Question It Answers Typical Owner What a Miss Can Cost


Quote comparison (before bind) Comparison Competing carrier quotes for the same risk Which option best fits the client's exposures and budget? Producer or account manager Recommending the wrong coverage type or inadequate limits


Bind-order verification (at bind) Checking Binder against the quote the client accepted Did we bind what the client chose? Account manager Coverage bound on terms the client didn't agree to


Policy checking (after issuance) Checking Issued policy against the binder, quote, and application Does the policy match what was agreed? Account manager, CSR, or service team Failure to procure; an exclusion nobody caught


Renewal comparison (before renewal) Comparison Expiring policy against the renewal offer What changed, and does the client know? Account manager Coverage reductions the client was never told about


‍


‍


Two of the four tasks are checks and two are comparisons. The checks happen after a decision has been made, so any difference is an error to fix. The comparisons happen before a decision, so any difference is information for the client.


## **Where E&O risk sits in each**


Big "I" Swiss Re E&O program data from 2017–2022 ranks failure to procure coverage as the No. 1 reason agencies are sued, according to[IA Magazine](https://www.iamagazine.com/2024/01/08/how-the-hard-market-and-talent-shortages-compound-agency-eo-exposures/) . The next most common causes were failing to adequately explain or disclose policy provisions, giving the carrier inaccurate information, failing to recommend the correct type of coverage, and failing to recommend adequate values or limits.


Those causes, plus the administrative errors Big "I" now ranks third, split along the same line as the two workflows:


‍


Leading E&O Claim Cause Workflow That Addresses It How It Helps


Failure to procure coverage Bind-order verification and policy checking Confirms the bound and issued coverage matches what the client requested


Failing to adequately explain or disclose policy provisions Quote and renewal comparison Surfaces the differences the client needs to hear about and acknowledge


Providing inaccurate information to the carrier Policy checking Reviews the policy against the application, exposing details recorded incorrectly


Failing to recommend the correct type of coverage Quote comparison Puts coverage forms and exclusions side by side before the client chooses


Failing to recommend adequate values or limits Quote and renewal comparison Shows limit and deductible changes across options and against expiring terms


Administrative errors Policy checking Catches wrong names, dates, and locations before the policy reaches the client


‍


The pressure isn't easing. In early 2025, Big “I” Professional Liability’s E&O operations lead[told IA Magazine](https://www.iamagazine.com/2025/05/01/whats-driving-the-rise-in-eo-claims-and-what-can-your-agency-do-to-prevent-one/) that the program had seen an uptick in both the frequency and severity of E&O claims over the previous six months, with failure to procure still the top loss driver and administrative errors the third largest. For more on catching form problems early, see our guide to[endorsement and form checks before submission](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/broker-compliance-review-software) .


## **Which one does your brokerage need first?**


For most brokerages, policy checking comes first. It has a clear pass-or-fail standard, it maps directly to the leading cause of E&O claims, and it applies to every bound policy, so the volume is predictable. Comparison becomes the priority when the book is in motion: a remarketing push, a carrier exit, or a soft market where clients shop on price.


Adoption data shows where agencies stand. The Big "I" 2026 Agency Universe Study found that[46% of agencies use AI](https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/national/2026/09/24/886639.htm) , up from 15% in 2024, with coverage form analysis (43%) and contract reviews (35%) among the reported uses. In March 2026, Insurance Journal reported that a Big "I" Agents Council for Technology (ACT) survey found that[far fewer agencies use AI in policy comparison tools](https://www.insurancejournal.com/magazines/mag-features/2026/03/09/860642.htm) (20%). Liberty Mutual's 2026 Independent Agency Growth Study puts the payoff at[an average of four hours saved per week](https://www.iamagazine.com/news/agents-using-ai-save-4-hours-a-week-says-liberty-mutual-study/) for agents using AI.


Staffing is the other constraint. Agencies in the same Agency Universe Study listed finding and screening strong job candidates among their top challenges (45%). Manual checking and comparison compete for the same account manager hours, which is why many teams start with the task that runs on every policy and add comparison as capacity frees up. Teams with heavy renewal volume can also look at[automated renewal summaries](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/automated-policy-renewal-review-tools) and[renewal pack preparation tools](https://www.furtherai.com/blog/tools-automate-renewal-pack-brokers) .


## **How AI handles both on one desk**


Checking and comparison share their raw material: quotes, binders, policies, and endorsements. That makes them a natural fit for one AI system, as long as a person reviews the output. A[2023 E&O Report on AI in agencies](https://www.biginy.org/eo-report/) from Big I New York advises that an experienced employee oversee and double-check any AI policy-checking process, confirming the accuracy of its review.


FurtherAI's[Policy Check & Compare case study](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/policy-check-compare-ai-teammate) shows what this looks like at scale. A mid-sized insurer with over 1,500 employees and $1 billion in annual revenue deployed an AI teammate to review quotes, binders, and issued policies for coverage breadth, terms, exclusions, and endorsements, including "give-back" endorsements. Policy checks ran 20 times faster than the manual process, and side-by-side comparisons ran 30 times faster with equal or superior accuracy. Manual review time fell by up to 95%, and the insurer reported 400% ROI within months. The same comparisons gave its brokers detailed side-by-side views of coverage.


On the brokerage side,[Leavitt Group](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/leavitt-group) uses FurtherAI for account manager workflows that include proposal building, policy checking, document comparison, and loss run analysis. A loss run of more than 130 lines went from hours to minutes, with consistent results in production over six months. Quote comparison also sits next to proposal building. One large national MGA that uses FurtherAI to compare carrier quotes and assemble proposals cut proposal time by 75%, producing[proposals in under 10 minutes](https://www.furtherai.com/customers/how-brokers-use-furtherai-to-generate-client-proposals-in-minutes) instead of 30–45.

## **Frequently asked questions**


#### What is the difference between policy checking and policy comparison?


Policy checking confirms that an issued policy matches what the client agreed to buy, by reviewing it against the binder, quote, and application. Policy comparison lines up two or more documents, such as competing quotes or an expiring policy and its renewal offer, to show how they differ. Checking looks for errors to correct. Comparison gives the broker a list of differences to explain so the client can make an informed choice.


#### When should a broker check a new policy?


Check a new policy as soon as it arrives from the carrier, before you deliver it to the client. Utica National's E&O guidance stresses prompt checking, so errors surface while they're still easy to correct. Review the named insured, addresses, policy period, limits, forms, and endorsements against the binder and quote, and repeat the check whenever an endorsement changes the policy mid-term.


#### Is quote comparison the same as policy comparison?


Quote comparison is one type of policy comparison. It lines up competing carrier quotes for the same risk before the client chooses a carrier. Renewal comparison is the other common type, lining up the expiring policy against the renewal offer. Both produce a list of differences in limits, deductibles, exclusions, and endorsements that the broker explains to the client, ideally with written acknowledgment of any reductions in coverage.


#### How does policy checking reduce E&O risk?


Failure to procure coverage is the No. 1 reason agencies are sued, based on Big "I" Swiss Re E&O program data. Policy checking catches the errors behind many of those claims: a missing location, a lower limit than the one bound, or an endorsement that narrows coverage. Finding them before delivery gives the broker time to get a corrected policy from the carrier, before the client discovers the gap at claim time.


#### Can AI handle both policy checking and policy comparison?


Yes. Both tasks read the same documents, so one AI system can extract terms from quotes, binders, and policies, then flag mismatches or list differences. In FurtherAI's Policy Check & Compare case study, an insurer ran policy checks 20 times faster and side-by-side comparisons 30 times faster than manual work. E&O counsel still recommends that an experienced employee review AI output before it reaches the client.


#### Do small agencies need dedicated policy checking software?


Small agencies carry the same E&O exposure as large ones, with fewer people to absorb manual checking. A saved checklist and a consistent process are the starting point. Dedicated software is worth evaluating when policy volume outgrows the team's time, when checks get skipped during renewal season, or when the agency moves many accounts to new carriers, a scenario Utica National links to at least one-third of agency E&O claims.
